title: When People Thought Worms Caused Cavities

sections.name: When People Thought Worms Caused Cavities
lines: For thousands of years, people believed toothaches were caused by a tiny worm, living inside your tooth.
The tooth worm was blamed for holes, and for the pain. People thought you could feel it wriggling.
Some healers burned seeds near the mouth, and then pointed at tiny worm-like shapes left behind, as proof.
They were actually just the burnt seeds' sprouts.
In 1728, a French dentist, Pierre Fauchard, said there was no such thing.
We now know it's bacteria, feeding on sugar and making acid. Much smaller than a worm.
